description: F-CORE-043: the audit trail stops being append-only merely BECAUSE NO CODE PATH DELETES FROM IT and becomes checkable. That distinction is the whole point — the old guarantee was a property of the procedure, so an auditor had to read the source or trust the deployment, and docs/gobd-conformance.md §13 says plainly that a direct UPDATE against a summae_* table left no trace at all. Since format 0.8 every record carries the hash of its predecessor over canonical JSON (RFC 8785), and `auditTrailIntegrity` walks the chain. WHY THE TRAIL AND NOT THE JOURNAL: a chain over the postings would need `previousEntryHash`, which datenformat.md reserves — writers must not populate it in v0.x and readers MUST ignore it, so a chain there would be evidence for nobody (SPEC-022). THE ERASURE IS THE HARD PART and the reason the last steps exist: a record erased under a privacy right leaves a SHELL that keeps both hashes, never a hole. Deleting the row would break the link at its successor for good, so every later verification would report a manipulation that never happened — and a warning that is always on is a warning nobody reads. The shell's own content can no longer be verified against its hash, which is exactly what an erasure means; `redacted` counts them so nobody reads the difference as a silent pass. This fixture also runs against the DATABASE subject, which is where it earns its keep: the adapter chains at append and rewrites shells at erasure, and until it did, in-memory and persisted trails disagreed while every other fixture stayed green.

expect.comment: One record went — and it went by being replaced, not removed.

`intact` is the answer an auditor wants; the three counts are why it is that answer. `unchained: 0` because this tenant was born at 0.8 — a trail carried over from an older format would report its pre-0.8 records here and NOT as breaks, which is the distinction that keeps the check usable after an upgrade. `redacted: 1` is published rather than folded into `chained`, so a shell is never mistaken for a verified record.
The shell does not leak into the change history: it carries the reserved objectType `redacted`, so a question about a partner cannot reach it. What remains about this partner is the erasure itself.
